hook.spoken: Entry eight. The venue Wi-Fi just died.

voiceover: Entry eight. The venue Wi-Fi just died. Norah's Notebook, entry eight. The story is fiction. The fix is real. Last time: the line at the front door finally moved. Dear notebook: two days until Mara and Eli's wedding. Final walk-through. The garlands glow, and the signal's gone. Eli's phone spins. Mara's phone spins. The router blinks, and that's all. Mara asks the only question that matters. What if this is Saturday? Here's what I'd do: a wedding day backup plan, in three layers. Plan A is the signal. You can't control it. Plan B is a check-in page that's already open. Open Wedillybird's check-in page before doors open, while you still have signal. If the signal drops, each scan waits in a queue on the phone. The screen reads check-ins pending sync, until the signal returns. If the page was never opened, it can't help. Here's the part people skip: test it in airplane mode first. If a winter wedding is on your list, follow along. Tomorrow: planners, one calm status per couple. Plan C is paper. A paper list of confirmed guests, in alphabetical order. One pen, and one lead who decides. One rule for the door: let people in first, and tick them off after. Print the timeline too, and hand it to every vendor. Timeline guides say send it at least two weeks ahead. Inside two weeks? Send it today. Today still counts. Saturday's whole plan now fits on two pages. At nine, the signal returns, and the queued scan syncs. I'm Norah, an AI character, and this is Wedillybird. The pen crosses out the signal, and writes the next problem. Guests arrive early.

Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment:
Entry 08 recap (the story is fiction, the tips are real). A wedding day backup plan in three layers:
Plan A: the venue signal. You can't control it.
Plan B: open your check-in page before doors open, while you have signal, and test it in airplane mode first. If the page was never opened, it can't help.
Plan C: a paper list of confirmed guests in alphabetical order, one pen, one lead who decides. Let people in first, tick them off after.
Also hand the printed day-of timeline to every vendor, at least two weeks ahead (Joy and Zola timeline guides, 2026). If you're inside two weeks, send it today.
Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).

needs_proof: S09 offline beat must be a real recording: phone in airplane mode, a staged code scanned, the 'check-ins pending sync' badge, then back online and the sync message (r1b open item 5, r3 B2). If it is unavailable or unconvincing, replace the two SCREEN beats with a title card 'Scans wait in a queue. They sync when the signal returns.': the voice-over alone carries the meaning.
Never present this as working with no signal at all: the page must already be open (r3 section 0 row 8). The voice-over says so twice (open it first; if it was never opened, it can't help).
r2 T49 states 'at least two weeks' in its core insight (Joy) next to Zola's one-month checklist item: re-read both pages before posting.
claims_review.notes: Fiction: 'two days to go', the dead router, 'nine' and every conversation are story elements, never results. Offline wording follows r3 E6 (keep checking guests in when the signal drops; scans sync when back online): no 100 percent claim, no 'works offline', no counts or speeds, no encryption. The only r2 figure is T49's two-week lead for sharing the timeline; the advice to test in airplane mode, keep a paper list and 'let people in first' is practical advice in Norah's voice ('here's what I'd do'), not a sourced statistic. Product beat is S09 offline queue only (about 8 s) and still makes sense if replaced by a card. Competitor names appear only as an on-screen source. Closing ritual follows entries 01-02: AI line, pen line, cliffhanger card last; the follow CTA with the teaser sits mid-video.
